verses.text: David built houses for himself in the City of David. He also prepared a place for God's ark and set up a tent for it.
Then David said, "No one except the Levites may carry God's ark. The LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD and to serve him forever."
David gathered all Israel in Jerusalem to bring the LORD's ark up to the place he had prepared for it.
He called together the descendants of Aaron and the Levites:
From the descendants of Kohath, Uriel the leader and one hundred and twenty of his relatives.
From the descendants of Merari, Asaiah the leader and two hundred and twenty of his relatives.
From the descendants of Gershom, Joel the leader and one hundred and thirty of his relatives.
From the descendants of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the leader and two hundred of his relatives.
From the descendants of Hebron, Eliel the leader and eighty of his relatives.
From the descendants of Uzziel, Amminadab the leader and one hundred and twelve of his relatives.
Then David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.

He said to them, "You are the heads of the Levite families. You and your relatives must make yourselves holy, so you can bring the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, up to the place I have prepared for it.
The first time, you Levites did not carry it, and so the LORD our God burst out in anger against us. We did not ask him how to do it the right way."
So the priests and Levites made themselves holy, so they could bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.
The Levites carried God's ark on their shoulders with the poles, just as Moses had commanded by the LORD's word.
David told the leaders of the Levites to appoint some of their relatives as singers. They were to play musical instruments, lyres, harps, and cymbals, and sing loud, joyful songs.
So the Levites appointed Heman son of Joel, his relative Asaph son of Berechiah, and from their relatives the Merarites, Ethan son of Kushaiah.
With them were their relatives next in rank: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, and the gatekeepers Obed-Edom and Jeiel.
The singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were to play loud bronze cymbals.
Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah were to play harps tuned to a high pitch, called Alamoth.
Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were to lead with lyres tuned to a low pitch, called Sheminith.
Chenaniah, a leader of the Levites, was in charge of the singing. He taught the singers because he was skilled at it.
Berechiah and Elkanah were to guard the ark.
The priests Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer were to blow trumpets in front of God's ark. Obed-Edom and Jehiah were also to guard the ark.
So David, the leaders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went with great joy to bring the ark of the LORD's covenant up from Obed-Edom's house.
Because God helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the LORD's covenant, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
David was wearing a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites carrying the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah, who led the singing. David was also wearing a linen ephod.
So all Israel brought up the ark of the LORD's covenant with shouts of joy, with the sound of rams' horns and trumpets, and with loud cymbals, harps, and lyres.
As the ark of the LORD's covenant came into the City of David, Saul's daughter Michal looked out of a window. When she saw King David dancing and celebrating, she hated him in her heart.
